objects.name: Mercury
objects.what: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun: a year lasts 88 days. No air to speak of, 430 °C by day and -180 °C at night.

objects.name: Venus
objects.what: Earth's size, but under a crushing carbon-dioxide atmosphere at 465 °C: the hottest planet. No spacecraft is working there right now.

objects.name: Earth
objects.what: Home. Everything else on this map was launched from here.

objects.name: Mars
objects.what: A cold desert world half Earth's width, with the busiest fleet of robots anywhere beyond Earth.

objects.name: Jupiter
objects.what: The giant: more than twice the mass of all other planets together, with nearly a hundred known moons. Four of them are worlds of their own.

objects.name: Saturn
objects.what: The ringed giant. Its moon Titan has rivers and seas of liquid methane; its moon Enceladus sprays water into space.

objects.name: Uranus
objects.what: An ice giant tipped on its side. Visited once, by Voyager 2 in 1986.

objects.name: Neptune
objects.what: The farthest planet: a year lasts 165 Earth years. Visited once, by Voyager 2 in 1989.

objects.name: Ceres
objects.what: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the nearest dwarf planet. NASA's Dawn orbited it from 2015 to 2018 and is still circling it, switched off.

objects.name: Vesta
objects.what: The second-largest asteroid, bright enough to see without a telescope at times. Dawn orbited it in 2011-2012.

objects.name: Psyche (asteroid)
objects.what: A metal-rich asteroid 220 km wide, perhaps the stripped core of a world that never finished forming. The Psyche spacecraft arrives in 2029.

objects.name: Apophis
objects.what: A 340-metre asteroid that will pass closer than our weather satellites on 13 April 2029, visible to the naked eye. It will not hit. OSIRIS-APEX will be there.

objects.name: Didymos
objects.what: A small asteroid with a moon, Dimorphos. In 2022 NASA's DART hit the moon on purpose and changed its orbit: the first planetary-defence test. Hera is on its way to inspect the result.

objects.name: Pluto
objects.what: The best-known dwarf planet, with a heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice. New Horizons flew past in 2015.

objects.name: Eris
objects.what: A dwarf planet as big as Pluto, right now nearly three times farther away. Finding it in 2005 led to the new definition of "planet".

objects.name: Haumea
objects.what: An egg-shaped dwarf planet that spins once every four hours, with rings and two moons.

objects.name: Makemake
objects.what: A reddish dwarf planet beyond Pluto, found in 2005.

objects.name: Sedna
objects.what: A red world on an 11,000-year orbit that never comes near the planets. Nobody knows for sure how it got there.

objects.name: 2026 ED138
objects.what: A large distant object found in 2026 with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, and a dwarf-planet candidate. Space Lab measured it on photographic plates from 1954 to 1991 (Asteroids tab).

objects.name: Halley's Comet
objects.what: The most famous comet, back every 76 years. It passed its farthest point from the Sun in 2023, beyond Neptune, and returns in 2061.

objects.name: 3I/ATLAS
objects.what: The third known visitor from another star, found in July 2025. It passed the Sun in October 2025 and is leaving for good.

objects.name: Voyager 1
objects.what: The farthest thing humans have made. It flew past Jupiter and Saturn, crossed into the space between the stars in 2012, and still phones home with a 23-watt radio. It carries a golden record of sounds and pictures from Earth.

objects.name: Voyager 2
objects.what: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune. In interstellar space since 2018 and still sending data, with instruments being switched off one by one to save power.

objects.name: Pioneer 10
objects.what: The first spacecraft through the asteroid belt and past Jupiter (1973). Silent since 2003, coasting towards the star Aldebaran. Its position here is worked out, not tracked.

objects.name: Pioneer 11
objects.what: The first spacecraft to fly past Saturn (1979). Silent since 1995. Its position here is worked out, not tracked.

objects.name: New Horizons
objects.what: Flew past Pluto in 2015 and the small world Arrokoth in 2019, and keeps going through the Kuiper belt, measuring dust and the Sun's thinning wind.

objects.name: Parker Solar Probe
objects.what: Flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere, closer than anything before it: 6 million km from the surface, at up to 690,000 km/h, the fastest object ever built. It studies why the corona is so hot and where the solar wind starts.

objects.name: Solar Orbiter
objects.what: Takes the closest pictures of the Sun, and is tilting its orbit to look down on the Sun's poles, which had never been seen.

objects.name: STEREO-A
objects.what: Circles the Sun slightly faster than Earth, so it sees the Sun from the side: a second viewpoint for solar storms heading our way.

objects.name: SOHO
objects.what: Has watched the Sun without a break since 1996 from a spot 1.5 million km sunward of Earth. Also the most successful comet finder ever: over 5,000, many spotted by volunteers.

objects.name: BepiColombo
objects.what: Two orbiters travelling together to Mercury: Europe's to map the surface and interior, Japan's to study its magnetic field. After eight years and nine planet flybys they enter orbit around Mercury on 21 November 2026.

objects.name: JUICE
objects.what: On its way to Jupiter's icy moons Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, which hide oceans under their ice. Arrives in 2031 and will be the first spacecraft to orbit a moon of another planet (Ganymede).

objects.name: Europa Clipper
objects.what: Will fly past Jupiter's moon Europa about 50 times from 2030 to find out whether the ocean under its ice could support life. The largest planetary spacecraft NASA has built.

objects.name: Lucy
objects.what: Touring the Trojan asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit, leftovers from when the planets formed. It reaches the first group in 2027.

objects.name: Psyche (spacecraft)
objects.what: Travelling to the metal-rich asteroid Psyche with solar-electric engines; it arrives in 2029.

objects.name: Hera
objects.what: Going back to the asteroid pair Didymos and Dimorphos to measure exactly what NASA's DART impact did in 2022, so the method can be trusted if an asteroid ever needs deflecting. It arrives at the end of 2026.

objects.name: OSIRIS-APEX
objects.what: As OSIRIS-REx it brought pieces of asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023. Renamed, it now heads for asteroid Apophis and will arrive just after its close pass of Earth in April 2029.

objects.name: Hayabusa2
objects.what: Brought samples of asteroid Ryugu to Earth in 2020 and kept going: it is on its way to a tiny, fast-spinning asteroid it will reach in 2031.

objects.name: Juno
objects.what: In orbit around Jupiter since 2016, flying over its poles. It showed that Jupiter's core is fuzzy rather than solid and photographed the moons Io, Europa and Ganymede up close.

objects.name: James Webb Space Telescope
objects.what: The largest telescope in space, with a 6.5-metre gold mirror. It sees infrared light: the first galaxies, stars being born inside dust clouds, and the air of planets around other stars. It sits 1.5 million km from Earth, on the side away from the Sun.

objects.name: Euclid
objects.what: Maps billions of galaxies across a third of the sky to work out what dark matter and dark energy are doing to the universe.

objects.name: TESS
objects.what: Watches patch after patch of sky for the tiny dips when a planet crosses its star. Space Lab searches its data every night (TESS hunter tab). It loops around Earth every 13.7 days.

objects.name: Gaia
objects.what: Measured the positions and motions of nearly two billion stars, the map most of astronomy now rests on. Retired in March 2025 and parked in an orbit around the Sun. Space Lab uses its catalogue daily.

objects.name: Spitzer
objects.what: An infrared telescope that worked until 2020 and found, among much else, most of the seven planets of TRAPPIST-1. It trails behind Earth, drifting slowly away.

objects.name: Kepler
objects.what: Stared at one patch of sky and showed that planets are everywhere: over 2,700 confirmed. Out of fuel since 2018, it follows Earth around the Sun.

objects.name: Tesla Roadster
objects.what: A car. It was the dummy load of the first Falcon Heavy rocket and has been circling the Sun ever since, out past Mars and back.
